think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 9-year-old boy presented with severe knee pain following a minor fall, superimposed on months of indolent knee discomfort and constitutional B-symptoms. Physical examination showed knee swelling without erythema or warmth (classic "tumor albus" / cold abscess). Imaging revealed a distal femoral metaphyseal lytic lesion breaching the cortex and growth plate into the joint. Initial surgical drainage, bacterial/fungal cultures, and initial TB PCR were negative, leading to initial misclassification and delayed recognition of osteoarticular tuberculosis.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Following admission physical examination, inflammatory markers, plain radiographs, and knee MRI demonstrating the distal metaphyseal osseous lesion with physeal extension and cortical breach, immediately prior to surgical incision, drainage, and send-out microbiologic and histopathologic testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis / septic arthritis (expected with cortical breach and joint fluid), brucellosis, and autoinflammatory conditions (FMF, rheumatic fever). Differentiated by indolent non-erythematous swelling, negative initial pyogenic cultures and rheumatologic workup, and repeat surgical debridement revealing cheese-like caseous tissue with acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen staining.
case_prompt: A 9-year-old boy, medically free, presented to the emergency department with severe right knee pain of 1 day's duration after a fall, superimposed on a progressive onset of right knee discomfort over the course of many months. The pain was accompanied by intermittent fevers up to 38.5 °C, general weakness, weight loss, anorexia, night sweats, malaise, and fatigue. There was no personal or family history of chronic infectious illnesses. On physical examination, there was right knee swelling and tenderness without redness or warmth. He was able to bear weight, and hip and knee joints demonstrated a full range of motion. Laboratory testing showed hemoglobin 12 g/dL, white blood cell count 8,500/μL (neutrophils 57%), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 60 mm/h, and C-reactive protein (CRP) 17.2 mg/L. Plain chest radiography was normal. Plain radiography of the right knee revealed an osseous lesion at the distal femoral metaphysis. Contrast-enhanced MRI of the right knee demonstrated an osseous lesion at the distal metaphysis with growth plate and epiphyseal involvement, along with cortical breach and fistula formation.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Acute or subacute pyogenic osteomyelitis / septic arthritis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Initially suspected due to post-traumatic exacerbation, elevated inflammatory markers, and cortical breach with joint fluid; however, the knee lacked erythema and heat, broad-spectrum antibiotics (teicoplanin and imipenem) failed to prevent recurrence, and routine aerobic/anaerobic cultures remained sterile.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The histopathological reports from the surgically extricated tissue and pus showed signs of acute and chronic inflammation. The TB PCR was negative, and all cultures were negative for Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Brucellosis and autoinflammatory syndromes (FMF / Rheumatic fever)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given regional endemicity in Jordan and presentation with subacute febrile monoarthritis and systemic symptoms; ruled out by negative serological and autoinflammatory evaluations.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: All tests, including those for Brucella titer, familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), rheumatic fever, and viral workup, came out negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Recurrence of symptoms led to repeat surgical debridement, revealing classic cheese-like caseous tissue and necrotizing granulomas with acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: the Ziehl-Nelsen stain showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammatory tissue with strains of acid-fast bacilli. After that, the diagnosis of osteoarticular tuberculosis was confirmed

editor_comments: Admission triage boundary preserves the diagnostic tension of pediatric tumor albus. Verbatim quotes verified.
